news.title: Patna civic body to hold property tax camps across wards
news.para: Starting October 5, Patna Municipal Corporation will host ward-specific property tax assessment camps. These sessions aim to evaluate unassessed holdings and rectify the tax records. Homeowners are encouraged to attend to clear any outstanding dues and avert potential penalties. This initiative is part of an extended door-to-door survey designed to boost revenue collection, with sanitation inspectors earmarking properties for assessment.

news.title: Rajasthan government notifies rural land conversion rules, moves approvals online
news.para: Starting November 2, 2026, Rajasthan is set to launch new regulations for the conversion of agricultural land to non-agricultural purposes. Applications can be submitted via a centralized online portal for efficiency. The fee structure varies: residential units will cost Rs 2,000, while other types will attract a Rs 20,000 fee.

news.title: Visakhapatnam civic body to streamline building permissions, water supply connections
news.para: In a recent meeting, GVMC's chief city planner A Prabhakar Rao assured developers that the town planning department is actively resolving building permission issues. This includes streamlining the application process for greater efficiency. Superintending engineer Pallam Raju addressed water supply connection procedures, while developers voiced concerns that officials responded to, elaborating on regulations and timelines for future projects. GVMC is committed to providing ongoing support to builders and developers.

news.title: New housing launches slow as developers in Goa turn cautious
news.para: In Panaji, the launch of new residential projects is stalled as developers grapple with escalating construction costs and uncertain regulations. Following a post-pandemic boom, the market is now experiencing reduced sales and growing unsold inventory. Local buyers are feeling the squeeze, with affordability declining despite stagnant prices. Some developers are opting to hold off on new ventures until clearer policies emerge, though a handful remain hopeful about future market dynamics.

news.title: Pune: Yerawada MHADA residents protest stalled redevelopment, demand mini-clusters
news.para: Residents of Yerawada are voicing dissatisfaction with the halted redevelopment project by MHADA, advocating for the creation of smaller housing clusters. They argue that the current mega-cluster proposal fails to ensure the necessary resident agreement, affecting over 3,500 homes. Their recent protest demonstrates a pressing need for faster solutions to unsafe living conditions.

news.title: Telangana clears registrations of non-NALA houses in 22-A relief move
news.para: The government of Telangana has announced a memo aimed at easing the registration process of homes built on converted residential lands. This initiative seeks to resolve the longstanding 22-A disputes that have hindered property owners. District collectors will be tasked with verifying applications to ensure compliance with the necessary NALA charges, ultimately providing relief for families previously unable to sell their homes due to these registration barriers.

news.title: Telangana government raises fire NOC height limit for apartments to 24 metres
news.para: The Telangana fire department is increasing the height limit for provisional Fire NOC regarding residential buildings. The new limit will be changed from 18m to 24m and will come into effect from October 7. This adjustment will simplify the approval process for lower and mid-rise apartments. However, safety measures such as emergency exits and firefighting systems will still be monitored during construction.

news.title: Homebuyers of Supertech projects worried over constant delay to approach Supreme Court
news.para: Homebuyers of 16 stalled housing projects by Supertech are planning to approach the Supreme Court again. They are frustrated with the lack of progress since NBCC took over construction nearly two years ago. According to buyers, the delay has severely affected their living situations, as many flats remain undelivered. NBCC has proposed a timeline for construction to begin by January 2027, citing various regulatory challenges.

news.title: Tens of thousands protest across Spain over housing crisis
news.para: Massive protests erupted across Spain as tens of thousands rallied for urgent action on the ongoing housing crisis. The government's housing proposals faced rejection from opposition parties, leading to significant unrest. Frustrated demonstrators demanded that their needs be prioritized, calling for a nationwide strike. While Valencia experienced violent clashes between police and protesters, other cities maintained a peaceful atmosphere.

news.title: Chandigarh civic body turns C&D waste into over ₹50 lakh revenue in six months
news.para: The Municipal Corporation in Chandigarh has turned construction and demolition waste into sand, bricks, and aggregate. From April to September, the civic body received over 2,700 metric tonnes of waste, which is processed for reuse. The authority earned between Rs 5 lakh to Rs 10 lakh monthly by selling these materials to government agencies. Despite multiple attempts to find a private bidder, the facility operates on a no-profit, no-loss basis.

news.title: Panaji residents seek rejection of five NBCC projects over infrastructure limits
news.para: Residents of Panaji have voiced their concerns over five redevelopment projects by NBCC due to insufficient infrastructure. A letter to Mayor Rohit Monserrate highlights issues with drainage, water supply, and electricity. People for Panaji’s secretary, Chryselle Dias, criticized the government for its apparent double standards regarding development approvals. Citizens urge careful examination of the city’s rainfall deficits and existing infrastructure challenges before proceeding with these projects.

news.title: Uttarakhand GST department recovers ₹2.25 crore as tax evasion from Eden Senior Living & Wellness
news.para: Following a thorough inspection of Eden Senior Living & Wellness by the Uttarakhand tax department, it became evident that discrepancies in GST payments had occurred. The company responded by depositing Rs 2.25 crore towards its identified tax liability of Rs 12.50 crore, mainly stemming from improper input tax credit usage.

news.title: India retail leasing falls 4.4% to 2.22 million sq ft in Q3 2026: Report
news.para: Retail leasing across India's top eight cities stood at 2.22 million sq ft in Q3 2026, down 7.3% sequentially and 4.4% year-on-year, while Grade A mall vacancy declined to 4.8%. About 12.7 million sq ft of new mall supply is expected through 2028.

news.title: Office, mall occupancies likely to approach 90% by March 2027: Report
news.para: Occupancy across India’s top office markets is expected to reach 88.5-89% by March 2027, while Grade A malls are likely to maintain occupancy of around 88-88.5%, supported by GCC-led office demand, retailer expansion and healthy leasing activity.

news.title: Iris scan, Aadhaar app if fingerprint fails during property registration in Maharashtra
news.para: Beginning October 1, it will be essential to use Aadhaar-based identity verification for property registrations covering a wide array of documents. To assist senior citizens and those with fingerprints that cannot be read, options like iris scanning and an Aadhaar application will be available. This new approach is designed to combat fraudulent registrations while decreasing the need for witnesses during transactions.

news.title: Saroj Poddar Group, Keventer launch ₹400 crore real estate debt AIF
news.para: Poddar Keventer Capital Advisors has launched a Category II alternative investment fund with a target corpus of ₹400 crore and a ₹200 crore greenshoe option. The fund will invest in secured real estate debt opportunities across Delhi-NCR and West Bengal.

news.title: Gurugram: Registrar asks Mahindra Aura RWA to follow conveyance deeds, bye-laws on EWS access
news.para: Disputes over access to parks and internal roads at Mahindra Aura in Gurgaon have escalated. The residents' welfare association has been ordered to comply with registered documents regarding common spaces. EWS residents claim harassment and restrictions on movement within the complex. Despite the RWA’s arguments, complaints have been raised regarding discriminatory treatment against EWS residents. Affected residents intend to challenge the RWA's decisions in the appropriate forums.

news.title: Noida: Allottees challenge ATS’s revised Sports City plan over nine commercial sites
news.para: Concerns are mounting among allottees of the ATS Kinghood Drive project over the modified Sports City layout plan. They argue that the new design permits unauthorized commercial developments, undermining established land use agreements. Only a minor portion of land designated for commercial use remains, raising alarm as the project is only 60% complete.

news.title: Some slum dwellers can’t hold SRA project to ransom: Bombay high court
news.para: The Bombay High Court has decided not to enforce a directive for Ruparel Buildcon's removal from a major redevelopment initiative, which encompasses a sprawling 16-acre area with various slum societies. Disputes have arisen concerning the consent of some slum residents, leading to complicated legal dynamics. The court underscored the necessity for state authorities to effectively handle public lands and tackle slum rehabilitation issues.
